title: Let a dwelling for non-hosted short-term rental for no more than 180 days a year without consent
what: In Greater Sydney and the other prescribed areas, a dwelling let as non-hosted short-term rental accommodation is exempt development only if it is used that way for no more than 180 days in a 365-day period; beyond that it needs development consent.

sources.title: State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021 (NSW)
sources.quote: 112 Exempt development—non-hosted short-term rental accommodation (1) Development for the purpose of non-hosted short-term rental accommodation is exempt development for the purposes of this Policy if— (a) the dwelling meets the general requirements, and (b) for a dwelling located in a prescribed area—the dwelling is not used for non-hosted short-term rental accommodation for more than 180 days in a 365-day period,

triggers.note: Letting a dwelling as non-hosted short-term rental accommodation

reach.condition: if it lets a dwelling in a prescribed area for non-hosted short-term rental

confidence_note: The Policy's own words set the 180-day limit for exempt development. Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the official text (28 February 2025), which is not itself official.

assessment.summary: A code of conduct, a mandatory register, fire safety rules and a 180-night cap on unhosted stays in Greater Sydney. It limits short-term rental supply and protects hotels from some competition; effects on long-term rental supply are not weighed here.

marks.reason: A 180-night cap on unhosted stays in Greater Sydney limits supply from hosts.
Hosts must register and meet fire safety and code requirements.
